# Push back a story, and propose its rewrite

A story the suite can't check as written goes back to its person (stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md, "Push
back when"). Send it back with the reason, and, when you can, the story rewritten so it can be checked:
the person accepts it by deleting what is above it, so the next pass implements it.

## 1. Append the push-back

Never change the person's text. Append, and leave the file in stories/new/:

```
---- PUSHBACK (2026-10-05) ----
Not implemented: <one sentence: why>.
Needed:
- <exactly what would make it implementable, one line each>
```

**A suggestion says what it rests on.** When you offer the person something to confirm (an outcome, a
split, which of two pages), write it as yours and name where you saw it: "I suggest <the outcome>,
because <the crawled page, a saved page, the story's own words> shows <what it shows>." One with nothing
behind it says so: "I suggest <the outcome>, from the story's words only; no page here shows it." The
person knows the business: when they correct you, the source you named shows which record was wrong.

## 2. Propose a rewrite, when one can be checked

Below the push-back, append the story as it could be implemented, under this line, exactly:

```
---- PROPOSED REWRITE (accept: delete everything above this line, this line too; or correct it first) ----
<id, exactly as the file name writes it> <title>
As a <who>, I want <what>, so that <why>.
Start on <the page, in the words a visitor sees: a link's text, a heading; never a class or a call>.
<one step per line, each a link, button or field in the words on the page; never a locator or data-testid>
Then <one outcome a visitor can see on the page it ends on>.
```

A rewrite that needs something only the person can decide (a permission, a choice between two things
you name) says so on its own line under its title, `Needs from you: ...`: accepting keeps that line, and
the next pass reads it with the person's `Answer:` under it. Never a value the site takes any of (a word
to type, a made-up name): choose one yourself, write it in the step, and say it is made up.

A rewrite can be checked when **every** line holds:

- **The same business intent.** It asks for what the person wanted, in words this suite knows. Never
  drop the hard part to make it easy: if the only story you could check is a different one, write no
  rewrite and say so in the push-back. A story already narrowed once (an earlier rewrite, the person's
  own edit) is not narrowed again without saying what it has become.
- **One outcome**, seen at the end. A story pushed back whole has no criterion that can be checked as
  written (a story with some that can is implemented, criterion by criterion: stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md,
  4.). Its rewrite keeps its criteria as a numbered list, each one rewritten so it can be checked, in the
  story's order. Count what a visitor sees at the end, not the lines: steps, conditions and the page's
  arrival are not outcomes.
- **The step makes the difference.** The outcome is false before the steps and true after them, on the
  page as the crawl saw it. Opening a page is a step: what it shows then (its rows, its columns, its
  links, a heading's words) is an outcome, and a story that only opens a page keeps it. Not an outcome:
  what every test already checks as the page opens (its title, the browser tab's words, and what its page
  class's "Proven loaded by" line names; anything else, a heading's words included, is checked only by a
  test of its own), a message or section there
  before the click, a list already in the order the sort asks for (read the crawled page: its order as opened is where a test starts). Say in the
  push-back what the page shows before the step, so the person sees why. When the page already shows on
  arrival what the step would make (a message open, a value typed), the rewrite undoes it first, then does
  the step: close the message, then make a new one; its return is the outcome. That is the same story, not
  a different one.
- **What a visitor reads.** The outcome is something on the page a visitor reads (a title, a price, a
  row), not the address or "the page is the right one": a story about what a page shows checks what it
  shows.
- **The id as the file name has it** (`pe-018`, never `PE-018`): a second spelling in the text is a
  second id.
- **Every name matches exactly one thing** in ai/GLOSSARY.md, controls/ or the page as crawled (never
  something only an unseen page would hold, like what a click adds: then write none, below): the
  rewrite is where the vague word becomes the exact one ("Contact Us" becomes "the Contact Us link in
  the footer").
- **Data by its name in the suite** (SiteConfig, the test data files); a value the site must know (a
  login, an order number) is never made up. A throwaway one (a word to type) you choose, and say so.
- **Nothing sent on the live site** unless the team's rules allow it.

## 3. Write no rewrite when only a person can answer

A page the crawl never saw and no saved page shows, a decision about what the site should do, permission
to send a form, an account or data the suite lacks: these the push-back asks for, and no rewrite can
supply. Then append, instead of a rewrite, this line, exactly, and nothing after it (a sketch of the
story you would write belongs above it, in Needed, with each part only the person can give left as a
blank in angle brackets: "Then <the words the saved page shows>"; never filled with a guess):

```
---- PROPOSED REWRITE: none (only you can give what is needed above) ----
```

## 4. Then

Do not implement your own rewrite: the person judges it first. A story file that still holds a
`---- PROPOSED REWRITE` line is waiting on its person: leave it, and list it in your report as waiting,
unless an `Answer:` line under the rewrite accepts it. `PROPOSED REWRITE: none` is never accepted: it proposes nothing.
